\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{میانبر} (miyânbor)}{میانبر (miyânbor)}]{\fa{میانبر} (miyânbor) — a shortcut}

\label{lesson:FA-C448-miyanbor}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for main, then the Persian for side.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{میانبر}}
\textbf{\fa{میانبر}} (\emph{miyânbor}) — \textquotedblleft{}a shortcut\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{راننده} \fa{از} \fa{یک} \fa{میانبر} \fa{رفت} \fa{و} \fa{زود} \fa{رسیدیم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Rânande az yek miyânbor raft va zud residim.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The driver took a shortcut and we arrived early.
\end{quote}

\emph{miyân} 'middle' + \emph{bor} 'cutting'.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{miyânbor} is a native compound of inherited words: \emph{miyân} 'middle', usually traced to Middle Persian \emph{mayān}, and \emph{bor}, the present stem of \emph{boridan} 'to cut': a way that cuts through the middle.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{miyânbor}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{miyânbor}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{miyânbor}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for main, then the Persian for side, then say \emph{miyânbor} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{سربالایی} (sarbâlâyi)}{سربالایی (sarbâlâyi)}]{\fa{سربالایی} (sarbâlâyi) — an uphill slope, a climb}

\label{lesson:FA-C448-sarbalayi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for side, then the Persian for a shortcut.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{سربالایی}}
\textbf{\fa{سربالایی}} (\emph{sarbâlâyi}) — \textquotedblleft{}an uphill slope, a climb\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{دوچرخه} \fa{سواری} \fa{در} \fa{سربالایی} \fa{سخت} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Docharkhe-savâri dar sarbâlâyi sakht ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Cycling uphill is hard.
\end{quote}

\emph{sar} 'head' + \emph{bâlâ} 'up' + \emph{-i}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{sarbâlâyi} is a native compound of \emph{sar} 'head', from Middle Persian \emph{sar} (EtymDB), and \emph{bâlâ} 'up', usually traced to Middle Persian \emph{bālāy}, with the ending \emph{-i}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for side, then the Persian for a shortcut, then say \emph{sarbâlâyi} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{سرازیری} (sarâziri)}{سرازیری (sarâziri)}]{\fa{سرازیری} (sarâziri) — a downhill slope, a descent}

\label{lesson:FA-C448-saraziri}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a shortcut, then the Persian for an uphill slope.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{سرازیری}}
\textbf{\fa{سرازیری}} (\emph{sarâziri}) — \textquotedblleft{}a downhill slope, a descent\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{در} \fa{سرازیری} \fa{ماشین} \fa{تند} \fa{میرود}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Dar sarâziri mâshin tond miravad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Going downhill the car goes fast.
\end{quote}

The opposite of \emph{sarbâlâyi}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{sarâziri} is usually analysed as native \emph{sar} 'head' and a form of \emph{zir} 'under, down', with the ending \emph{-i}: head-downwards. EtymDB does not list the compound.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{زیرگذر} (zirgozar)}{زیرگذر (zirgozar)}]{\fa{زیرگذر} (zirgozar) — an underpass; a pedestrian subway}

\label{lesson:FA-C448-zirgozar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for an uphill slope, then the Persian for a downhill slope.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{زیرگذر}}
\textbf{\fa{زیرگذر}} (\emph{zirgozar}) — \textquotedblleft{}an underpass; a pedestrian subway\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{برای} \fa{رد} \fa{شدن} \fa{از} \fa{اتوبان} \fa{از} \fa{زیرگذر} \fa{رفتیم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Barâ-ye rad shodan az otobân az zirgozar raftim.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
To cross the motorway we went through the underpass.
\end{quote}

\emph{zir} 'under' + \emph{gozar} 'passage'.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{zirgozar} is a native compound of \emph{zir} 'under', which EtymDB lists, and \emph{gozar} 'passage', the present stem of \emph{gozashtan} 'to pass'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{روگذر} (rugozar)}{روگذر (rugozar)}]{\fa{روگذر} (rugozar) — a flyover, an overpass}

\label{lesson:FA-C448-rugozar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a downhill slope, then the Persian for an underpass.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{روگذر}}
\textbf{\fa{روگذر}} (\emph{rugozar}) — \textquotedblleft{}a flyover, an overpass\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{روی} \fa{روگذر} \fa{ترافیک} \fa{سنگین} \fa{بود}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Ru-ye rugozar terâfik sangin bud.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The traffic on the flyover was heavy.
\end{quote}

\emph{ru} 'over' + \emph{gozar} 'passage'; the opposite of \emph{zirgozar}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{rugozar} is a native compound of \emph{ru} 'face, on top' and \emph{gozar} 'passage', the present stem of \emph{gozashtan} 'to pass', which is inherited: EtymDB traces it to a Middle Persian verb 'to pass, to cross'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
